southIndianStatus.productLedExplanation: Oma Podi is the South Indian sev — a thin besan-rice flour sev flavored with ajwain (omam in Tamil), which is the characteristic South Indian digestive spice. It originates from Tamil Nadu as the thinner, digestive-spiced version of North Indian sev.
southIndianStatus.flavorLedExplanation: The ajwain (omam) flavor is the South Indian differentiator — North Indian sev uses carom seeds or turmeric; Oma Podi uses the same spice in a more prominent, front-and-center application that makes the South Indian flavor identity unmistakable.
southIndianStatus.overallSummary: Oma Podi is South India's answer to bhujia — same thin sev format, but with ajwain (omam) as the flavor signature instead of moth dal or turmeric. Product-led with a deep Tamil identity, a staple in the Diwali mixture and as a standalone tea-time snack.

stateSpeciality.origin: Oma Podi developed from the broader South Indian sev tradition as a specific variation flavored with omam (ajwain), which was already widely used in Tamil cooking for its digestive properties. The name 'Oma' literally refers to the spice omam (ajwain).
stateSpeciality.culturalSignificance: Oma Podi is a core component of South Indian Diwali Mixture (kara mixture) and is consumed as a standalone snack. It appears in nearly every South Indian home's snack stock.
stateSpeciality.storytelling: Oma Podi is the sev that South India made its own. The ajwain — called omam in Tamil — is not a garnish. It is the flavor anchor. A Tamil kitchen without a stash of oma podi is a kitchen that has not been properly stocked. It goes into the Diwali mixture, it crumbles into hot rasam, it pairs with filter coffee in the afternoon. It is the most versatile thing in the tin.
stateSpeciality.bestSeason: Year-round, with peak during Diwali for mixture preparation.

positioning.brandLadderRationale: Oma Podi is the quintessential Daily Rituals product — everyday, tea-time, year-round, no occasion dependency.

functionalCallouts.explanation: Ajwain (omam) contains thymol — a documented digestive enzyme stimulant used in Ayurveda for centuries. Oma Podi's primary flavor is also its most functional ingredient.
Traditional Oma Podi uses only besan (chickpea flour) and rice flour — no refined wheat flour (maida). This makes it a lighter, more digestible snack than maida-based alternatives.

productDescriptors.title: The Sev South India Made Its Own
productDescriptors.descriptor: North India has its bhujia. South India has oma podi — the same thin sev format, different soul. The ajwain (omam in Tamil) is not a flavoring afterthought. It is the reason this exists as a separate snack. It is also, not coincidentally, the spice Paati kept in the medicine cabinet for stomach aches. This sev digests you while you're eating it.
productDescriptors.principle: DISTINCTIVENESS + GEOGRAPHICAL PROVENANCE (Shotton Bias 4 + Sutherland S3)
productDescriptors.rationale: Positioning oma podi as 'the sev South India made its own' creates a clear identity distinction from North Indian bhujia using the geographical and cultural separation that Sutherland's provenance principle recommends.

productDescriptors.title: The Diwali Mixture Anchor
productDescriptors.descriptor: South Indian Diwali Mixture is not one snack. It is a composition — and every composition has an anchor. Oma podi is the anchor. The thin, crispy, ajwain-forward sev that brings everything together: the murukku bits, the peanuts, the boondhi, the banana chips shards. Take the oma podi out and the mixture becomes a collection of things. Put it in and it becomes Diwali.
productDescriptors.rationale: Positioning oma podi as the ingredient that makes the mixture a 'Diwali mixture' — and framing its absence as a downgrade — is classic loss aversion applied to an ingredient's role in a larger composition.
